column1: # Images WITHDRAWN from quay.io/aarchbio, and why.
# Withdrawal means the repository was deleted, so a pull of the ref now fails with
# "manifest unknown" instead of succeeding and handing the user a container that
# cannot execute. A loud failure at pull time beats a silent one at run time: our
# provenance labels are only readable AFTER a pull, so they cannot warn anybody.
# Only done where the tool's OWN primary binary is the wrong architecture, i.e.
# nothing in the image works. Images that merely lose a sub-feature are kept —
# prokka and plasmidid are fully functional apart from GenBank submission, and
# withdrawing them would destroy more value than it protects.
# The digest is recorded so the decision is auditable and so the exact artifact
# could be rebuilt if upstream ever fixes the package.
# Columns (tab-separated):  repo  tag  digest  date  reason
pureclip
column5: Both of its own binaries (bin/pureclip, bin/winextract) are x86-64 in an arm64-tagged image: 0 of 2 usable. bioconda publishes pureclip 1.3.1 under subdir linux-aarch64 while shipping x86-64 payloads, and 1.3.1 is the only version with any aarch64 claim. Nothing to fall back to. bioconda-recipes#69811.

column1: glnexus
column5: bin/glnexus_cli is its only binary and is x86-64: 0 of 1 usable. Same mislabeled-subdir cause, and 1.4.1 is the only version claiming aarch64. bioconda-recipes#69811.

column1: oncocnv
column5: Its CNV-calling step cannot run. oncocnv BUNDLES lib/R/library/cghseg itself (its own conda record owns the x86-64 cghseg.so - not inherited from r-cghseg as first reported), and processSamples.R, the step that calls copy number, references cghseg 8 times; processControl.R and perChrVisualization.R reference it 0 times. No fix path: no aarch64 cghseg exists anywhere - bioconda's r-cghseg is noarch with an x86-64 .so and conda-forge does not package it - so there is nothing for a postinstall repair to reinstall. Only count extraction and the control baseline survive, which is not what the tool is for. bioconda-recipes#69811.
